output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses is most likely caused by the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not by agency nurses. The new server imported only 3 of 14 forwarding rules. The 11 skipped rules included a 15-second hold-off for short oxygen-level dips, suppression of repeats, and sending probe-off alarms only to the charge nurse. Since then, Pods A–C nurses get about twice as many phone alerts (80+ vs 38 per shift) and take about twice as long to acknowledge them. Pod D still uses the old server and shows no change, even though its agency share is similar. Within Pods A–C, core and agency nurses were affected equally. Raw monitor alarm counts did not change, which argues against higher acuity and against the September monitor update. Do not cap agency nurses or open performance reviews; this would blame the wrong people. Do not switch off phone forwarding either. Restore the old rules, with clinical validation and committee sign-off, and track phone alerts per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Moving Pod D to the new server should wait until its rules are fixed. Access-point installation is premature. The rise in sick leave is plausibly linked to alert overload, but that link is not proven; the virus season is a rival explanation. I am fairly confident (about 90%) in the main finding.
